sentences.zh: 律曆中

translations.literal: Measures and the Calendar, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatises on Measures and the Calendar, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 夫曆者，紀陰陽之通變，極往數以知來，可以迎日授時，先天成務者也。

translations.literal: Now the calendar is that which records the transformations through yin and yang, exhausts past numbers to know what is to come, can meet the sun and grant the seasons, and accomplishes tasks before Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar records the ceaseless transformations of yin and yang, extrapolates from past reckonings to anticipate the future, aligns human affairs with the sun's course, and thus enables one to act ahead of Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 然則懸象著明，莫大於二曜，氣序環複，無信於四時。

translations.literal: Thus among the suspended images that show brightness, none is greater than the two luminaries; among the cyclical sequences of qi, none is more trustworthy than the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Among the celestial signs that hang in the heavens, none shines more brilliantly than the sun and moon; among the patterns by which vital force moves through the year, none is more reliable than the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 日月相推而明生矣，寒暑迭進而歲成焉，遂能成天地之文，極乾坤之變。

translations.literal: The sun and moon push each other and brightness is born; cold and heat advance in turn and the year is completed—thus they can complete the pattern of Heaven and Earth and exhaust the transformations of qian and kun.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon drive one another in their courses and light comes into being; cold and heat succeed each other until the year is complete. In this way the pattern of Heaven and Earth is fulfilled and the full range of cosmic change is realized.

sentences.zh: 天數五，地數五，五位相乘而各有合。

translations.literal: The numbers of Heaven are five; the numbers of Earth are five. The five positions multiply each other and each has its pairing.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has five numbers and Earth has five numbers; when these five positions are multiplied together, each pair combines in its proper way.

sentences.zh: 天數二十有五，地數三十，凡天地之數五十有五，所以成變化而行鬼神也。

translations.literal: The numbers of Heaven total twenty-five; the numbers of Earth total thirty. In all, the numbers of Heaven and Earth are fifty-five—by this changes are accomplished and spirits and ghosts are set in motion.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's numbers sum to twenty-five and Earth's to thirty, giving fifty-five in all—the number by which transformation is achieved and the workings of spirits are carried out.

sentences.zh: 乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策一百四十有四，凡三百六十，以當期之日也。

translations.literal: The tally-sticks of qian number two hundred and sixteen; those of kun number one hundred and forty-four—in all three hundred and sixty, corresponding to the days of one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: The tally-sticks for qian total two hundred and sixteen, and those for kun one hundred and forty-four—three hundred and sixty altogether, matching the days of a full cycle.

sentences.zh: 至乃陰陽迭用。

translations.literal: Thus yin and yang are used in alternation.
translations.idiomatic: In this way yin and yang alternate in their operation.

sentences.zh: 剛柔相摩，四象既陳，八卦成列，此乃造文之元始，創曆之厥初者歟？

translations.literal: Hard and soft rub against each other; the four images are already arrayed and the eight trigrams stand in rows—is this not the primal beginning of creating the written pattern and the very first origin of establishing the calendar?
translations.idiomatic: Hard and soft interact, the four emblems take their places, and the eight trigrams stand in order—is this not the primal source of written pattern and the very beginning of calendrical reckoning?

sentences.zh: 洎乎炎帝分八節，軒轅建五部，少昊以鳳鳥司曆，顓頊以南正司天，陶唐則分命和仲，夏後乃備陳《鴻范》，湯武革命，咸率舊章。

translations.literal: Down to the time when the Flame Emperor divided the eight seasonal nodes, the Yellow Emperor established the five departments, Shaohao used the phoenix bird to manage the calendar, Zhuanxu used the southern director to manage Heaven, Taotang then separately appointed He and Zhong, the Xia dynasty later fully set forth the "Great Plan," and Tang and Wu changed the mandate—all followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: From the Flame Emperor, who divided the eight seasonal nodes, through the Yellow Emperor, who established the five bureaus; from Shaohao, who entrusted the calendar to the phoenix bird, and Zhuanxu, who set the southern director to oversee Heaven; from Yao, who appointed He and Zhong, to the Xia, who fully codified the Great Plan—through the revolutions of Tang and Wu, all followed established calendrical precedent.

sentences.zh: 然文質既殊，正朔斯革，故天子置日官，諸侯有日禦，以和萬國，以協三辰。

translations.literal: Yet since literary ornament and substance differ, the new year's month and day were changed; therefore the Son of Heaven established sun officials, and the feudal lords had sun stewards, to harmonize the myriad states and to align the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as ritual forms changed from age to age, so did the calendar's new year and first month; hence the Son of Heaven appointed officials of the sun, and feudal lords maintained their own calendrical officers, to harmonize the myriad states and keep the three celestial markers in accord.

sentences.zh: 至於寒暑晦明之徵，陰陽生殺之數，啟閉升降之紀，消息盈虛之節，皆應躔次而不淫，遂得該浹生靈，堪輿天地，開物成務，致遠鉤深。

translations.literal: As for the signs of cold and heat, darkness and brightness, the numbers of yin-yang generation and destruction, the records of opening and closing, rising and falling, and the nodes of waxing and waning, fullness and emptiness—all responded to the sequence of celestial stations without excess, and thus could comprehensively reach all living beings, support Heaven and Earth, open up things and accomplish tasks, and reach far and probe deep.
translations.idiomatic: The signs of cold and heat, light and dark, the reckoning of yin and yang's generative and destructive phases, the cycles of opening and closing and of rising and falling, and the rhythms of waxing and waning—all matched the celestial stations without deviation. Thus the calendar could embrace all living things, span Heaven and Earth, open the way for human enterprise, and reach to the farthest depths.

sentences.zh: 周德既衰，史官廢職，疇人分散，禨祥莫理。

translations.literal: When the virtue of Zhou had declined, the historiographers abandoned their duties, calendar specialists scattered, and auspicious and inauspicious signs were no longer investigated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's virtue waned, the historiographers neglected their duties, calendrical experts dispersed, and no one any longer attended to omens and portents.

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，頗推五勝，自以獲水德之瑞，以十月為正。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm, it largely promoted the theory of the five conquests, considered itself to have obtained the auspicious sign of the Water Virtue, and took the tenth month as the new year.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin conquered the realm, it embraced the theory of cyclical conquest among the five phases, claimed the auspicious token of the Water Virtue, and made the tenth month the year's beginning.

sentences.zh: 漢氏初興，多所未暇，百有餘載，猶行秦曆。

translations.literal: When the Han house first rose, many things were not yet attended to; for more than a hundred years it still used the Qin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han dynasty's early years, many reforms went unattended, and for more than a century the Qin calendar remained in use.

sentences.zh: 至於孝武，改用夏正。

translations.literal: As for Emperor Xiaowu, he changed to use the Xia new year.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, the dynasty adopted the Xia calendar's first month as the new year.

sentences.zh: 時有古曆六家，學者疑其紕繆，劉向父子，咸加討論，班固因之，采以為志。

translations.literal: At that time there were six schools of ancient calendars; scholars doubted their errors, and Liu Xiang and his son both added discussions; Ban Gu followed them and selected their material for his treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Six ancient calendrical schools were then in circulation, and scholars questioned their inaccuracies. Liu Xiang and his son examined them thoroughly, and Ban Gu drew on their work for his treatise.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，未能詳考。

translations.literal: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, he was unable to examine matters in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the Han, no thorough calendrical review was undertaken.

sentences.zh: 逮于永平之末，乃複改行四分，七十餘年，儀式方備。

translations.literal: By the end of the Yongping era, the Quarter-Remainder calendar was again adopted; after more than seventy years, the procedures were finally complete.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the end of the Yongping reign was the Quarter-Remainder calendar reinstated; only after more than seventy years were its procedures fully established.

sentences.zh: 其後覆命劉洪、蔡邕，共修律曆，司馬彪用之以續《班史》。

translations.literal: Afterward they again ordered Liu Hong and Cai Yong jointly to revise the pitch pipes and calendar; Sima Biao used their work to continue the History of Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Hong and Cai Yong were again commissioned to revise the standards of pitch and calendar, and Sima Biao incorporated their work into his continuation of Ban Gu's history.

sentences.zh: 當塗受命，亦有史官，韓翊創之于前，楊偉繼之於後，咸遵劉洪之術，未及洪之深妙。

translations.literal: When the House of Cao received the mandate, it also had historiographers; Han Yi created a calendar before, and Yang Wei succeeded afterward—both followed Liu Hong's methods but did not reach Hong's profound subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cao Wei dynasty took power, it too maintained calendrical officers: Han Yi devised a system first, and Yang Wei followed, both adopting Liu Hong's methods but falling short of his depth and refinement.

sentences.zh: 中、左兩晉，迭有增損。

translations.literal: In the two Jin dynasties, Eastern and Western, there were successive additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Under both the Western and Eastern Jin, the calendar underwent repeated revisions.

sentences.zh: 至於西涼，亦為蔀法，事蹟糾紛，未能詳記。

translations.literal: As for Western Liang, it also had an obscuration-cycle method; the records are tangled and cannot be noted in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Western Liang likewise employed an obscuration-cycle calendar, but the records are too confused to recount in detail.

sentences.zh: 宋氏元嘉，何承天造曆，迄于齊末，相仍用之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of the Song house, He Chengtian created a calendar; down to the end of Qi it was used in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song dynasty's Yuanjia era, He Chengtian devised a new calendar that remained in continuous use until the end of Qi.

sentences.zh: 梁武初興，因循齊舊，天監中年，方改行宋祖沖之《甲子元曆》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang first rose, he followed Qi's old ways; in the middle of the Tianjian era he finally changed to use the Jiazi Origin Calendar of Zu Chongzhi of the Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang came to power, he initially retained Qi's calendar; only in mid-Tianjian did he adopt Zu Chongzhi's Jiazi Origin Calendar from the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 陳武受禪，亦無創改。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, he also made no new changes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the throne, he introduced no calendrical innovations.

sentences.zh: 後齊文宣，用宋景業曆。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi used the calendar of Song Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi adopted the calendar of Song Jingye.

sentences.zh: 西魏入關，行李業興曆。

translations.literal: When Western Wei entered the passes, Li Yexing created a calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei entered the Guanzhong region, Li Yexing devised a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 逮于周武帝，乃有甄鸞造《甲寅元曆》，遂參用推步焉。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Zhen Luan created the Jiayin Origin Calendar, and it was then used together in astronomical computation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Zhen Luan created the Jiayin Origin Calendar, which was then adopted for calendrical computation.

sentences.zh: 大象之初，太史上士馬顯，又上《丙寅元曆》，便即行用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daxiang era, Senior Grand Astrologer Ma Xian again submitted the Bingyin Origin Calendar, and it was immediately put into use.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daxiang era, Senior Grand Astrologer Ma Xian submitted the Bingyin Origin Calendar, which was adopted at once.

sentences.zh: 迄於開皇四年，乃改用張賓曆，十七年，複行張胄玄曆，至於義寧。

translations.literal: Down to the fourth year of Kaihuang, the calendar of Zhang Bin was adopted; in the seventeenth year, the calendar of Zhang Zhouxuan was again used, down to the Yining era.
translations.idiomatic: fourth year of In of Kaihuang the calendar of Zhang Bin was adopted; in 17th year of Kaihuang that of Zhang Zhouxuan was restored, and it remained in use until the Yining era.

sentences.zh: 今采梁天監以來五代損益之要，以著於篇雲。

translations.literal: Now the essential additions and reductions of the five dynasties since Liang's Tianjian era are selected and set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: What follows selects the chief calendrical revisions of the five dynasties since Liang's Tianjian era and records them in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 梁初因齊，用宋《元嘉曆》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, following Qi, it used the Yuanjia Calendar of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Early Liang, following Qi, continued to use the Song dynasty's Yuanjia Calendar.

sentences.zh: 天監三年下詔定曆，員外散騎侍郎祖暅奏曰：「臣先在晉已來，世居此職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian an edict was issued to fix the calendar. Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant Zu Geng memorialized, saying: "Your servant's family has held this office generation after generation since Jin.
translations.idiomatic: third year of In of Tianjian an edict ordered the calendar to be fixed. Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant Zu Geng memorialized: "My family has held this office for generations, going back to the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 仰尋黃帝至今十二代，曆元不同，周天、斗分，疏密亦異，當代用之，各垂一法。

translations.literal: Looking up from the Yellow Emperor to the present through twelve generations, the calendar origins differ, and the circuits of heaven and dipper fractions vary in density and sparsity; each age that used them transmitted its own single method.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing from the Yellow Emperor down through twelve dynasties, each age has used a different calendar origin, with varying values for the celestial circuit and the dipper fraction; every dynasty in turn has handed down its own system.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，臣先人考古法，以為正曆，垂之於後，事皆符驗，不可改張。」

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song, your servant's forebear examined the ancient method and established it as the correct calendar, transmitting it to later ages; in all matters it matched verification and cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liu Song's Daming era, my ancestor examined the ancient method and established the correct calendar, transmitting it to posterity. Its predictions have always been verified, and it should not be changed."

sentences.zh: 八年，暅又上疏論之。

translations.literal: Close quotation. In the eighth year, Geng again submitted a memorial discussing it.
translations.idiomatic: eighth year of In of Tianjian, Zu Geng submitted another memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 詔使太史令將匠道秀等，候新舊二曆氣朔、交會及七曜行度，起八年十一月，訖九年七月，新曆密，舊曆疏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Astrologer Jiang Daoxiu and others to observe the qi and new moons, conjunctions, and motions of the seven luminaries of the old and new calendars, from the eleventh month of the eighth year to the seventh month of the ninth year; the new calendar was precise, the old calendar coarse.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Grand Astrologer Jiang Daoxiu and others to compare the old and new calendars by observing seasonal nodes, new moons, conjunctions, and the motions of the seven luminaries from the eleventh month of eighth year of Tianjian through the seventh month of ninth year of Tianjian. The new calendar proved accurate; the old one did not.

sentences.zh: 暅乃奏稱：「史官今所用何承天曆，稍與天乖，緯緒參差，不可承案。

translations.literal: Geng then memorialized, saying: "The He Chengtian calendar now used by the historiographers departs slightly from Heaven; the warp and woof are uneven and cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Geng then reported: "The He Chengtian calendar currently used by the historiographers already diverges from the heavens; its underlying principles are inconsistent and cannot be maintained.

sentences.zh: 被詔付靈台，與新曆對課疏密，前期百日，並又再申。

translations.literal: By edict it was sent to the Observational Platform to be compared with the new calendar for density and sparsity; the advance prediction was a hundred days, and it was verified again.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order it was sent to the Observational Platform to be tested against the new calendar. Predictions were made a hundred days in advance and verified twice over.

sentences.zh: 始自去冬，終於今朔，得失之效，並已月別啟聞。

translations.literal: From last winter down to this new moon, the results of success and failure have all been reported month by month.
translations.idiomatic: From last winter through the current new moon, the results have been reported month by month.

sentences.zh: 夫七曜運行，理數深妙，一失其源，則歲積彌爽。

translations.literal: Now the motions of the seven luminaries involve principles and numbers of profound subtlety; once the source is lost, errors accumulate year by year.
translations.idiomatic: The motions of the seven luminaries rest on principles of extraordinary subtlety; lose the underlying reckoning even once, and the error compounds with every passing year.

sentences.zh: 所上脫可施用，宜在來正。」

translations.literal: The submitted calendar may be put into use and should take effect from the coming new year.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar submitted may be adopted and should take effect from the coming new year."

sentences.zh: 至九年正月，用祖沖之所造《甲子元曆》頒朔。

translations.literal: Close quotation. In the first month of the ninth year, the Jiazi Origin Calendar created by Zu Chongzhi was used to promulgate the new moons.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of ninth year of Tianjian, Zu Chongzhi's Jiazi Origin Calendar was adopted and the new year's calendar was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 至大同十年，制詔更造新曆，以甲子為元，六百一十九為章歲，一千五百三十六為日法，一百八十三年冬至差一度，月朔以遲疾定其小餘，有三大二小。

translations.literal: By the tenth year of Datong, an imperial decree ordered a new calendar to be created, with jiazi as the origin, six hundred nineteen as the cycle year, one thousand five hundred thirty-six as the day divisor, one degree of winter solstice discrepancy over one hundred eighty-three years, and new moons determined by fast and slow motion for their small remainders, with three long months and two short months.
translations.idiomatic: tenth year of By of Datong an imperial decree ordered a new calendar: jiazi as the origin, 619 as the cycle year, 1,536 as the day divisor, one degree of precession at the winter solstice over 183 years, and new-moon small remainders determined by the moon's anomalistic motion, yielding three long months and two short months.

sentences.zh: 未及施用而遭侯景亂，遂寢。

translations.literal: Before it could be put into use, the rebellion of Hou Jing occurred, and the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could be implemented, Hou Jing's rebellion broke out, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 陳氏因梁，亦用祖沖之曆，更無所創改。

translations.literal: The Chen house followed Liang and also used the calendar of Zu Chongzhi, making no further innovations.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, following Liang, also used Zu Chongzhi's calendar without further modification.

sentences.zh: 後齊文宣受禪，命散騎侍郎宋景業葉圖讖，造《天保曆》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan of Later Qi received the abdication, he ordered Gentleman Attendant Song Jingye, relying on chart prognostications, to create the Tianbao Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi took the throne, he ordered Gentleman Attendant Song Jingye, drawing on prognostic charts, to create the Tianbao Calendar.

sentences.zh: 景業奏：依《握誠圖》及《元命包》，言齊受錄之期，當魏終之紀，得乘三十五以為蔀，應六百七十六以為章。」

translations.literal: Jingye memorialized: According to the "Chart of Grasping Sincerity" and the "Wrapping of the Primordial Mandate," the period when Qi would receive the register falls in the era when Wei ends; multiplying thirty-five gives the obscuration cycle, and six hundred seventy-six corresponds to the cycle year.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye reported that according to the Chart of Grasping Sincerity and the Wrapping of the Primordial Mandate, Qi would receive the mandate at the end of Wei's era; thirty-five multiplied yields the obscuration cycle, and 676 the cycle year."

sentences.zh: 文宣大悅，乃施用之。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Emperor Wenxuan was greatly pleased and put it into use.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan was delighted and ordered the calendar into use.

sentences.zh: 期曆統曰：「上元甲子，至天保元年庚午，積十一萬五百六算外，章歲六百七十六，度法二萬三千六百六十，斗分五千七百八十七，曆餘十六萬二千二百六十一。」

translations.literal: The calendar summary states: "From the upper origin jiazi to the first year of Tianbao, gengwu, the accumulated count is one hundred ten thousand five hundred six, outside the calculation; cycle year six hundred seventy-six, degree divisor twenty-three thousand six hundred sixty, dipper fraction five thousand seven hundred eighty-seven, calendar remainder one hundred sixty-two thousand two hundred sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar summary reads: "From the upper origin in jiazi to first year of Tianbao (gengwu), the accumulated count is 110,506 beyond the epoch; cycle year 676, degree divisor 23,660, dipper fraction 5,787, calendar remainder 162,261."

sentences.zh: 至後主武平七年，董峻、鄭元偉立議非之曰：「宋景業移閏於天正，退命於冬至交會之際，承二大之後，三月之交，妄減平分。

translations.literal: Close quotation. By the seventh year of Wuping under the Later Ruler, Dong Jun and Zheng Yuanwei submitted a dissenting opinion, saying: "Song Jingye shifted the intercalary month to the celestial new year, retreated the mandate to the moment of winter solstice conjunction, followed two long months, and at the third month's conjunction arbitrarily reduced the equal division.
translations.idiomatic: seventh year of In of Wuping under the last ruler, Dong Jun and Zheng Yuanwei objected: "Song Jingye shifted the intercalary month to the celestial new year, deferred the epoch to the winter solstice conjunction, placed it after two long months, and at the third month's conjunction arbitrarily reduced the equal division.

sentences.zh: 臣案，景業學非探賾，識殊深解，有心改作，多依舊章，唯寫子換母，頗有變革，妄誕穿鑿，不會真理。

translations.literal: Your servants find that Jingye's learning did not probe the hidden depths, and his understanding fell far short of deep comprehension; though intending to make changes, he largely followed old regulations, merely substituting son for mother with some alterations—arbitrary, forced, and contrived, not grasping true principle.
translations.idiomatic: We find that Jingye's learning did not reach to the hidden depths, and his understanding was shallow. Though he intended reform, he mostly followed old formulas, merely swapping one constant for another—a forced and arbitrary contrivance that misses true principle.

sentences.zh: 乃使日之所在，差至八度，節氣後天，閏先一月。

translations.literal: This caused the sun's position to err by as much as eight degrees, the seasonal nodes to lag behind Heaven, and the intercalary month to come one month early.
translations.idiomatic: The result was solar positions off by as much as eight degrees, seasonal nodes lagging behind the heavens, and intercalary months arriving a month too early.

sentences.zh: 朔望虧食，既未能知其表裡，遲疾之曆步，又不可以傍通。

translations.literal: For new and full moons and eclipses, he could neither know their inner and outer limits; the calendrical steps for fast and slow motion also could not be verified by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: For new and full moons and eclipses, he could not determine their limits; nor could his anomalistic reckoning be cross-checked by any alternative method.

sentences.zh: 妄設平分，虛退冬至，虛退則日數減于周年，平分妄設，故加時差於異日。

translations.literal: He arbitrarily set equal divisions and falsely retreated the winter solstice; false retreat made the day count less than a full year, and the arbitrary equal division caused the hour of occurrence to differ on different days.
translations.idiomatic: He arbitrarily imposed equal divisions and falsely shifted the winter solstice; this reduced the day count below a full year, and his arbitrary equal division caused the hour of occurrence to fall on the wrong day.

sentences.zh: 五星見伏，有違二旬，遲疾逆留，或乖兩宿。

translations.literal: The appearances and disappearances of the five planets deviated by as much as twenty days; their fast, slow, retrograde, and stationary motions sometimes missed by two lodges.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets' appearances and disappearances were off by as much as twenty days; their direct, retrograde, and stationary motions sometimes missed by two lunar lodges.

sentences.zh: 軌褵之術，妄刻水旱。

translations.literal: The method of orbital reckoning arbitrarily carved out floods and droughts.
translations.idiomatic: His orbital methods arbitrarily predicted floods and droughts.

sentences.zh: 今上《甲寅元曆》，並以六百五十七為章，二萬二千三百三十八為蔀，五千四百六十一為斗分，甲寅歲甲子日為元紀。」

translations.literal: Now we submit the Jiayin Origin Calendar, using six hundred fifty-seven as the cycle, twenty-two thousand three hundred thirty-eight as the obscuration, five thousand four hundred sixty-one as the dipper fraction, and the jiazi day of the jiayin year as the origin epoch.
translations.idiomatic: We now submit the Jiayin Origin Calendar, with 657 as the cycle year, 22,338 as the obscuration cycle, 5,461 as the dipper fraction, and the jiazi day of the jiayin year as the epoch."

sentences.zh: 又有廣平人劉孝孫、張孟賓二人，同知曆事。

translations.literal: Close quotation. There were also two men from Guangping, Liu Xiaosun and Zhang Mengbin, who jointly managed calendrical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two men from Guangping, Liu Xiaosun and Zhang Mengbin, also shared responsibility for calendrical matters.

sentences.zh: 孟賓受業于張子信，並棄舊事，更制新法。

translations.literal: Mengbin studied under Zhang Zixin; both abandoned the old system and created new methods.
translations.idiomatic: Mengbin had studied under Zhang Zixin; both men abandoned the old system and devised new methods.

sentences.zh: 又有趙道嚴，准晷影之長短，定日行之進退，更造盈縮，以求虧食之期。

translations.literal: There was also Zhao Daoyan, who measured the length and shortness of gnomon shadows to determine the sun's advance and retreat, and recreated the expansion-contraction tables to seek the dates of eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Daoyan measured gnomon shadows to determine the sun's advance and retreat, and reconstructed the solar anomaly tables to calculate eclipse dates.

sentences.zh: 劉孝孫以百一十九為章，八千四十七為紀，九百六十六為歲餘，甲子為上元，命日度起虛中。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosun took one hundred nineteen as the cycle, eight thousand forty-seven as the era, nine hundred sixty-six as the year remainder, jiazi as the upper origin, and set the sun's degree to begin at the middle of xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun used 119 as the cycle year, 8,047 as the era, 966 as the year remainder, jiazi as the upper origin, and set the solar degree to begin at the middle of the Xu lodge.

sentences.zh: 張孟賓以六百一十九為章，四萬八1千九百為紀，九百四十八為日法，萬四千九百四十五為斗分。

translations.literal: Zhang Mengbin took six hundred nineteen as the cycle, forty-eight thousand nine hundred as the era, nine hundred forty-eight as the day divisor, and fourteen thousand nine hundred forty-five as the dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengbin used 619 as the cycle year, 48,900 as the era, 948 as the day divisor, and 14,945 as the dipper fraction.

sentences.zh: 元紀共命，法略旨遠。

translations.literal: Their origin and era shared a single epoch; the method was concise in form but far-reaching in intent.
translations.idiomatic: Their origin and era shared a single epoch; the method was compact in form but far-reaching in design.

sentences.zh: 日月五星，並從斗十一起。

translations.literal: The sun, moon, and five planets all began from the eleventh degree of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, moon, and five planets all began from the eleventh degree of the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 盈縮轉度，陰陽分至，與漏刻相符，共日影俱合，循轉無窮。

translations.literal: Expansion-contraction and rotating degrees, yin-yang division and solstices, matched the clepsydra markings; together with the sun's shadow they all agreed, cycling without end.
translations.idiomatic: Solar anomaly tables, rotating degrees, and the yin-yang divisions at the solstices matched the clepsydra graduations; gnomon shadows agreed as well, cycling without end.

sentences.zh: 上拒春秋，下盡天統，日月虧食及五星所在，以二人新法考之，無有不合。

translations.literal: From the Spring and Autumn Annals above down to the Tian Tong calendar below, for solar and lunar eclipses and the positions of the five planets, when tested by the two men's new methods, none failed to match.
translations.idiomatic: From the Spring and Autumn period down through the Tian Tong calendar, when solar and lunar eclipses and the positions of the five planets were checked against their new methods, every case matched.

sentences.zh: 其年，訖幹敬禮及曆家豫刻日食疏密。

translations.literal: That year, down to Gan Jingli and the calendar specialists, they pre-calculated the density and sparsity of the solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gan Jingli and the calendrical specialists competed to predict the solar eclipse in advance.

sentences.zh: 六月戊申朔，太陽虧，劉孝孫言食于卯時，張孟賓言食于甲時，鄭元偉、董峻言食于辰時，宋景業言食于巳時。

translations.literal: On the wushen new moon of the sixth month, the sun was eclipsed. Liu Xiaosun said the eclipse would occur in the mao hour; Zhang Mengbin said the jia hour; Zheng Yuanwei and Dong Jun said the chen hour; Song Jingye said the si hour.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day new moon of the sixth month, a solar eclipse occurred. Liu Xiaosun predicted it for the mao hour, Zhang Mengbin for the jia hour, Zheng Yuanwei and Dong Jun for the chen hour, and Song Jingye for the si hour.

sentences.zh: 至日食，乃於卯甲之間，其言皆不能中。

translations.literal: When the eclipse came, it fell between the mao and jia hours; none of their predictions hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: When the eclipse came, it fell between the mao and jia hours; none of them was correct.

sentences.zh: 爭論未定，遂屬國亡。

translations.literal: The dispute was not settled before the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: The dispute was never resolved before the state fell.

sentences.zh: 臣案九章五紀之旨，三統四分之說，咸以節宣發斂，考詳晷緯，布政授時，以為皇極者也。

translations.literal: Your servant finds that the purport of the Nine Chapters and Five Records and the theories of the Triple Concordance and Quarter-Remainder all take regulating the seasons, issuing and gathering in, examining gnomon shadows and celestial coordinates, distributing government and granting the seasons, as the imperial pivot.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Chapters, Five Records, Triple Concordance, and Quarter-Remainder calendars all share one purpose: to regulate the seasons, measure gnomon shadows and celestial coordinates, govern the realm, and grant the proper seasons—the very pivot of imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 而乾維難測，斗憲易差，盈縮之期致舛，咎徵之道斯應。

translations.literal: Yet the qian axis is hard to measure, the dipper standard easily errs, the periods of expansion and contraction lead to mistakes, and the way of blame and portents responds accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the celestial axis is hard to measure, the dipper standard easily drifts, solar anomaly periods go awry, and calamities follow in their wake.

sentences.zh: 甯止蛇或乘龍，水能沴火，因亦玉羊掩曜，金雞喪精。

translations.literal: It is not only that snakes sometimes ride dragons and water can harm fire; thus also jade sheep dim their light and golden roosters lose their essence.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that snakes sometimes usurp the dragon's place and water overcomes fire; jade sheep dim their radiance and golden roosters lose their brilliance as well.

sentences.zh: 王化關以盛衰，有國由其隆替，曆之時義，于斯為重。

translations.literal: Royal transformation is tied to rise and decline; possession of a state depends on its flourishing and replacement; the timely significance of the calendar is weighty in this regard.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial fortunes rise and fall with the calendar; a dynasty's ascent and decline depend upon it. The calendar's timely significance could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 自炎漢已還，迄于有魏，運經四代，事涉千年，日禦天官，不乏於世，命元班朔，互有沿改。

translations.literal: From the blazing Han down to Wei, spanning four dynasties and involving a thousand years, sun stewards and celestial officers were never lacking in the world; fixing the origin and promulgating new moons were mutually revised and changed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han through Wei, across four dynasties and a millennium, calendrical officers were never absent from the court, yet the calendar origin and new-moon promulgation were revised again and again.

sentences.zh: 驗近則疊璧應辰，經遠則連珠失次，義難循舊，其在茲乎？

translations.literal: Tested at close range, stacked jades respond to the chronograms; traced over long distances, strung pearls lose their order—how can one follow the old? Is the answer here?
translations.idiomatic: Tested at close range, predictions may align; traced over centuries, they fall out of sequence. How can one simply follow precedent? The need for reform is clear.

sentences.zh: 大周受圖膺錄，牢籠萬古，時夏乘殷，斟酌前代，曆變壬子，元用甲寅。

translations.literal: Great Zhou received the chart and accepted the register, encompassing all antiquity; following Xia while riding Yin, it weighed the former ages; the calendar changed to renzi, and the origin used jiayin.
translations.idiomatic: Great Zhou received the mandate, embracing all antiquity; drawing on Xia and Yin, it weighed the achievements of former dynasties. Its calendar used renzi as the cycle and jiayin as the origin.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝索隱探賾，盡性窮理，以為此曆雖行，未臻其妙，爰降詔旨，博訪時賢，並敕太史上士馬顯等，更事刊定，務得其宜。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, the Martial Emperor, searched out the hidden and probed the depths, exhaustively examining nature and exhausting principle; he considered that though this calendar was in use, it had not reached perfection. Therefore he issued an edict, broadly consulting worthy men of the time, and also ordered Senior Grand Astrologer Ma Xian and others further to revise and fix it, striving to obtain what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, probing hidden principles to the utmost, judged that although this calendar was in use, it had not reached perfection. He issued an edict seeking advice from the finest scholars of the age and ordered Senior Grand Astrologer Ma Xian and others to revise it until it was right.

sentences.zh: 然術藝之士，各封異見，凡所上曆，合有八家，精粗踳駁，未能盡善。

translations.literal: Yet the masters of technique each sealed off different views; in all, eight schools submitted calendars, coarse and fine mixed together, unable to be entirely good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet calendrical experts held divergent views; eight schools in all submitted calendars, varying widely in quality, and none was fully satisfactory.

sentences.zh: 去年冬，孝宣皇帝乃詔臣等，監考疏密，更令同造。

translations.literal: Last winter, Emperor Xiaoxuan ordered your servants to supervise the testing of density and sparsity and further commanded us jointly to create a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter Emperor Xiaoxuan ordered us to supervise comparative testing and jointly devise a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 謹案史曹舊簿及諸家法數，棄短取長，共定今術。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the old registers of the historiography bureau and the numerical methods of the various schools, we discarded the short and took the long, jointly fixing the present method.
translations.idiomatic: We have examined the historiography bureau's old records and the numerical methods of all schools, discarded weaknesses and selected strengths, and jointly established the present system.

sentences.zh: 開元發統，肇自丙寅，至於兩曜虧食，五星伏見，參校積時，最為精密。

translations.literal: The origin opens its sequence, beginning from bingyin; as for the two luminaries' eclipses and the five planets' appearances and disappearances, when compared and verified over accumulated time, it is most precise.
translations.idiomatic: The epoch begins from bingyin; for eclipses of the sun and moon and the appearances and disappearances of the five planets, accumulated verification shows it to be the most precise.

sentences.zh: 庶鐵炭輕重，無失寒燠之宜，灰箭飛浮，不爽陰陽之度。

translations.literal: May the light and heavy of iron and charcoal not miss the fitness of cold and warmth; may the floating and sinking of ash arrows not err from the measure of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the iron-and-charcoal test will not miss the proper balance of cold and warmth, and the clepsydra's floating and sinking markers will not deviate from the measure of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 上元丙寅至大象元年己亥，積四萬一千五百五十四算上。

translations.literal: From the upper origin bingyin to the first year of Daxiang, jihai, the accumulated count is forty-one thousand five hundred fifty-four, on the calculation.
translations.idiomatic: From the upper origin in bingyin to first year of Daxiang (jihai), the accumulated count is 41,554.

sentences.zh: 日法五萬三千五百六十三，亦名蔀會法。

translations.literal: Day divisor fifty-three thousand five hundred sixty-three, also called the obscuration-conjunction divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Day divisor: 53,563, also called the obscuration-conjunction divisor.

translations.literal: Cycle year four hundred forty-eight, dipper fraction three thousand one hundred sixty-seven, obscuration divisor twelve thousand nine hundred ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: Cycle year: 448; dipper fraction: 3,167; obscuration divisor: 12,992.

sentences.zh: 章中為章會法。

translations.literal: Cycle medial is the cycle-conjunction divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The cycle medial serves as the cycle-conjunction divisor.

sentences.zh: 日法五萬三千五百六十三，曆餘二萬九千六百九十三，會日百七十三，會餘一萬六千六百一十九，冬至日在斗十二度。

translations.literal: Day divisor fifty-three thousand five hundred sixty-three, calendar remainder twenty-nine thousand six hundred ninety-three, conjunction days one hundred seventy-three, conjunction remainder sixteen thousand six hundred nineteen; the winter solstice sun is at the twelfth degree of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Day divisor: 53,563; calendar remainder: 29,693; conjunction period: 173 days; conjunction remainder: 16,619; winter solstice sun at the twelfth degree of the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 小周餘、盈縮積，其曆術別推入蔀會，分用陽率四百九十九，陰率九。

translations.literal: Small circuit remainder and expansion-contraction accumulation—the calendrical method separately computes entry into obscuration and conjunction, using yang rate four hundred ninety-nine and yin rate nine.
translations.idiomatic: Small circuit remainders and solar anomaly accumulations are computed separately for entry into obscuration and conjunction, using a yang rate of 499 and a yin rate of 9.

sentences.zh: 每十二月下各有日月蝕轉分，推步加減之，乃為定蝕大小餘，而求加時之正。

translations.literal: Below each of the twelve months there are rotating fractions for solar and lunar eclipses; by computation adding and subtracting these, one obtains the fixed large and small remainders of the eclipse and seeks the correct hour of occurrence.
translations.idiomatic: Below each of the twelve months are rotating eclipse fractions; by adding and subtracting these in computation, one obtains the fixed large and small remainders of the eclipse and determines the correct hour of occurrence.

sentences.zh: 其術施行。

translations.literal: This method was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: This method was adopted.

sentences.zh: 時高祖作輔，方行禪代之事，欲以符命曜於天下。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was serving as chief minister and was carrying out the affair of abdication and replacement; he wished to display mandate tokens to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozu was chief minister, preparing the transfer of the throne, and wished to display tokens of the mandate to the world.

sentences.zh: 道士張賓，揣知上意，自雲玄相，洞曉星曆，因盛言有代謝之徵，又稱上儀錶非人臣相。

translations.literal: The Daoist Zhang Bin, guessing the ruler's intent, claimed himself to have a mysterious countenance and thorough knowledge of stars and calendar; he therefore spoke at length of signs of dynastic succession and also said the ruler's bearing and appearance were not those of a mere subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Zhang Bin, sensing the ruler's intent, claimed mystical insight and mastery of astronomy and calendrics. He spoke at length of signs that the mandate was changing and declared that Gaozu's bearing was not that of a mere subject.

sentences.zh: 由是大被知遇，恆在幕府。

translations.literal: By this he was greatly favored and constantly remained in the military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby won great favor and remained constantly at Gaozu's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及受禪之初，擢賓為華州刺史，使與儀同劉暉、驃騎將軍董琳、索盧縣公祐、前太史上士馬顯、太學博士鄭元偉、前保章上士任悅、開府掾張撤、前蕩邊將軍張膺之、校書郎衡洪建、太史監候粟相、太史司曆郭翟、劉宜、兼算學博士張乾敘、門下參人王君瑞、荀隆伯等，議造新曆，仍令太常卿盧賁監之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of receiving the abdication, Bin was promoted to Inspector of Huazhou and ordered together with Palace Attendant Liu Hui, General of Flying Cavalry Dong Lin, Duke of Suolu County Gong You, former Senior Grand Astrologer Ma Xian, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Zheng Yuanwei, former Senior Preserver of Registers Ren Yue, Secretariat Aide Zhang Che, former General Who Sweeps the Border Zhang Yingzhi, Collator Heng Hongjian, Grand Astrologer Observer Su Xiang, Grand Astrologer Calendar Officer Guo Di, Liu Yi, Concurrent Erudite of Computational Learning Zhang Qianxu, Secretariat Attendant Wang Junrui, Xun Longbo, and others to discuss creating a new calendar; the Minister of Ceremonies Lu Fen was still ordered to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign, Gaozu promoted Zhang Bin to Inspector of Huazhou and commissioned him together with Liu Hui, Dong Lin, Gong You, the former Senior Grand Astrologer Ma Xian, Erudite Zheng Yuanwei, Ren Yue, Zhang Che, Zhang Yingzhi, Heng Hongjian, Su Xiang, Guo Di, Liu Yi, Zhang Qianxu, Wang Junrui, Xun Longbo, and others to devise a new calendar, with Minister of Ceremonies Lu Fen supervising the work.

sentences.zh: 賓等依何承天法，微加增損，四年二月撰成奏上。

translations.literal: Bin and the others followed He Chengtian's method with slight additions and reductions; in the second month of the fourth year the work was completed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin and his colleagues based their work on He Chengtian's method with minor modifications. In the second month of fourth year of Kaihuang they completed the calendar and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 高祖下詔曰：「張賓等存心算數，通洽古今，每有陳聞，多所啟沃。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an edict, saying: "Zhang Bin and the others set their hearts on computation and numbers, thoroughly versed in ancient and modern; whenever they submitted reports, they offered much enlightening counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu issued an edict: "Zhang Bin and his colleagues are devoted to computation, thoroughly versed in ancient and modern learning, and their reports have repeatedly offered valuable counsel.

sentences.zh: 畢功表奏，具已披覽。

translations.literal: The completed work has been memorialized and fully perused.
translations.idiomatic: Your completed memorial has been received and fully reviewed.

sentences.zh: 使後月複育，不出前晦之宵，前月之餘，罕留後朔之旦。

translations.literal: Thus the later month again conceives, not extending beyond the night before the last day of the month; the remainder of the earlier month rarely remains into the dawn of the later new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The following month begins its cycle without spilling past the last night of the month; the prior month's remainder rarely carries over to the next new-moon dawn.

sentences.zh: 減朓就朒，懸殊舊准。

translations.literal: Reducing the gibbous and approaching the crescent, it hangs far from the old standard.
translations.idiomatic: Adjusting from gibbous to crescent phase, it departs sharply from the old standard.

sentences.zh: 月行表裡，厥途乃異，日交弗食，由循陽道。

translations.literal: The moon's path has inner and outer aspects, and its course differs; when the sun crosses yet no eclipse occurs, it is because it follows the yang path.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's path has inner and outer aspects with differing courses; when the sun crosses the node yet no eclipse occurs, it is because the crossing follows the yang path.

sentences.zh: 驗時轉算，不越纖毫，逖德前修，斯秘未啟。

translations.literal: When tested by timely computation, it does not err by the slightest hair; the secret of earlier worthies' distant virtue had not yet been revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Verified by timely calculation, the error does not exceed a hair's breadth—a secret that earlier masters had not yet unlocked.

sentences.zh: 有一於此，實為精密，宜頒天下，依法施用。」

translations.literal: In any one of these respects, it is truly precise and should be promulgated throughout the realm and applied according to law."
translations.idiomatic: In each of these respects it is truly precise. It should be promulgated throughout the realm and put into use according to law."

translations.idiomatic: The essential parameters of Zhang Bin's calendar:

sentences.zh: 木精曰歲星，合率四千一百六萬三千八百八十九。

translations.literal: The essence of Wood is called the Year Star; its conjunction rate is forty-one million sixty-three thousand eight hundred eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Wood is Jupiter; its conjunction rate is 41,063,889.

sentences.zh: 火精曰熒惑，合率八千二十九萬七千九百二十六。

translations.literal: The essence of Fire is called the Sparkling Deluder; its conjunction rate is eighty million two hundred ninety-seven thousand nine hundred twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Fire is Mars; its conjunction rate is 80,297,926.

sentences.zh: 土精曰鎮星，合率三千八百九十二萬五千四百一十三。

translations.literal: The essence of Earth is called the Queller Star; its conjunction rate is thirty-eight million nine hundred twenty-five thousand four hundred thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Earth is Saturn; its conjunction rate is 38,925,413.

sentences.zh: 金精曰太白，合率六千一十一萬九千六百五十五。

translations.literal: The essence of Metal is called the Great White; its conjunction rate is sixty million one hundred nineteen thousand six hundred fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Metal is Venus; its conjunction rate is 60,119,655.

sentences.zh: 水精曰辰星，合率一千一百九十三萬一千一百二十五。

translations.literal: The essence of Water is called the Chronogram Star; its conjunction rate is eleven million nine hundred thirty-one thousand one hundred twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Water is Mercury; its conjunction rate is 11,931,125.

sentences.zh: 張賓所創之曆既行，劉孝孫與冀州秀才劉焯，並稱其失，言學無師法，刻食不中，所駁凡有六條：其一雲，何承天不知分閏之有失，而用十九年之七閏。

translations.literal: After the calendar created by Zhang Bin was put into use, Liu Xiaosun and the Ji Province scholar Liu Chuo both declared its errors, saying its learning had no master and its eclipse predictions missed the mark; their objections numbered six in all: First, they said He Chengtian did not know the error in distributing intercalary months and used seven intercalations in nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Bin's calendar was adopted, Liu Xiaosun and the Ji Province scholar Liu Chuo both challenged its errors, declaring that its methods lacked proper foundation and its eclipse predictions missed the mark. They raised six objections. First: He Chengtian did not recognize the error in distributing intercalary months and used the seven-intercalation-in-nineteen-years rule.

sentences.zh: 其二雲，賓等不解宿度之差改，而冬至之日守常度。

translations.literal: Second, they said Bin and the others did not understand the changing discrepancy in lodge degrees and kept the winter solstice at a fixed degree.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Zhang Bin and his colleagues did not account for the shifting discrepancy in lodge degrees and kept the winter solstice at a fixed position.

sentences.zh: 其三雲，連珠合璧，七曜須同，乃以五星別元。

translations.literal: Third, they said that when strung pearls and joined jades align, the seven luminaries must share the same origin, yet they set separate origins for the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Third: when the heavenly markers align, the seven luminaries must share a single origin, yet they assigned separate origins to the five planets.

sentences.zh: 其四雲，賓等唯知日氣餘分恰盡而為立元之法，不知日月不合，不成朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: Fourth, they said Bin and the others knew only that when the sun's qi remainder was exactly exhausted one could establish the origin method, but did not know that when sun and moon fail to conjoin, new-moon dawn and winter solstice cannot be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Zhang Bin and his colleagues knew only that when the solar qi remainder is exactly exhausted one may set the origin, but did not grasp that without sun-moon conjunction, new-moon dawn and winter solstice cannot be fixed.

sentences.zh: 其五雲，賓等但守立元定法，不須明有進退。

translations.literal: Fifth, they said Bin and the others merely adhered to the fixed method of establishing the origin and need not clarify advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Zhang Bin and his colleagues merely clung to a fixed origin method and did not account for advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 其六雲，賓等唯識轉加大餘二十九以為朔，不解取日月合會准以為定。

translations.literal: Sixth, they said Bin and the others knew only to add the rotating large remainder of twenty-nine to obtain the new moon, but did not understand taking sun-moon conjunction as the standard for fixing it.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Zhang Bin and his colleagues knew only to add the rotating large remainder of twenty-nine to obtain the new moon, but did not understand using sun-moon conjunction as the basis for fixing it.

sentences.zh: 此六事微妙，歷數大綱，聖賢之通術，而暉未曉此，實管窺之謂也。

translations.literal: These six matters are subtle; they are the great outline of calendrical reckoning and the common method of sages—yet Hui did not understand them; this is truly what is called viewing through a bamboo tube.
translations.idiomatic: These six points are subtle matters—the great framework of calendrical science and the common method of sages—yet Liu Hui did not grasp them. This was indeed viewing the heavens through a bamboo tube.

sentences.zh: 若乃驗影定氣，何氏所優，賓等推測，去之彌遠。

translations.literal: As for verifying shadows to fix the qi, the He family was superior; Bin and the others' deductions departed ever further.
translations.idiomatic: In verifying shadows to fix the seasonal nodes, He's method was superior; Zhang Bin's deductions strayed ever further.

sentences.zh: 合朔順天，何氏所劣，賓等依據，循彼迷蹤。

translations.literal: In conjunction with Heaven at new moon, the He family was inferior; Bin and the others followed and traced their mistaken tracks.
translations.idiomatic: In aligning new moons with Heaven, He's method was weaker; Zhang Bin followed and traced that mistaken path.

sentences.zh: 蓋是失其菁華，得其糠粃者也。

translations.literal: In general they lost the essence and got the chaff.
translations.idiomatic: In short, they discarded the essence and kept the chaff.

sentences.zh: 又雲，魏明帝時，有尚書郎楊偉，修《景初曆》，乃上表立義，駁難前非，雲：「加時後天，食不在朔。」

translations.literal: They also said that in the time of Emperor Ming of Wei, the Secretariat Gentleman Yang Wei revised the Jingchu Calendar and submitted a memorial setting forth principles, refuting earlier errors, saying: "The hour of occurrence lags behind Heaven, and the eclipse is not on the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: They also noted that under Emperor Ming of Wei, Secretariat Gentleman Yang Wei revised the Jingchu Calendar and submitted a memorial refuting earlier errors: "The hour of occurrence lags behind Heaven, and the eclipse does not fall on the new moon."

sentences.zh: 然觀楊偉之意，故以食朔為真，未能詳之而制其法。

translations.literal: Yet examining Yang Wei's intent, he therefore took eclipse-on-new-moon as true but was unable to explain it in detail and formulate the method.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei's intent was to treat eclipse-on-new-moon as the standard, but he could not fully explain it or formulate the method.

sentences.zh: 至宋元嘉中，何承天著曆，其上表雲：「月行不定，或有遲疾，合朔月食，不在朔望，亦非曆之意也。」

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, He Chengtian compiled a calendar; his submitted memorial said: "The moon's motion is not fixed; sometimes it is slow or fast. Conjunction and lunar eclipse do not fall on new or full moon—this also is not the calendar's intent."
translations.idiomatic: In the Liu Song's Yuanjia era, He Chengtian compiled a calendar whose submitted memorial stated: "The moon's motion is not uniform; it may be slow or fast. Conjunction and lunar eclipse do not always fall on new or full moon—this too departs from the calendar's intent."

sentences.zh: 然承天本意，欲立合朔之術，遭皮延宗飾非致難，故事不得行。

translations.literal: Yet Chengtian's original intent was to establish a method for conjunction, but he encountered Pi Yanzong's embellishment of error and provocation of difficulty, so the matter could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's original intent was to establish a conjunction method, but Pi Yanzong's obstruction prevented it from being implemented.

sentences.zh: 至後魏獻帝時，有龍宜弟複修延興之曆，又上表雲：「日食不在朔，而習之不廢，據《春秋》書食，乃天之驗朔也。」

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xian of Later Wei, Long Yidi again revised the Yanxing calendar and submitted a memorial saying: "Solar eclipses do not fall on the new moon, yet the practice is not abandoned; according to the Spring and Autumn Annals' records of eclipses, Heaven verifies the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xian of Later Wei, Long Yidi again revised the Yanxing calendar and submitted a memorial: "Solar eclipses do not fall on the new moon, yet the practice persists; according to the Spring and Autumn Annals' eclipse records, Heaven verifies the new moon."

sentences.zh: 此三人者，前代善曆，皆有其意，未正其書。

translations.literal: These three men were skilled calendrists of former ages; all had the right idea but did not correct their writings.
translations.idiomatic: These three were skilled calendrists of earlier ages; each had the right insight but failed to correct their written methods.

sentences.zh: 但歷數所重，唯在朔氣。

translations.literal: Yet what calendrical reckoning most values is only the new moon and the qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet calendrical reckoning values above all the new moon and the seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 朔為朝會之首，氣為生長之端，朔有告餼之文，氣有郊迎之典，故孔子命曆而定朔旦冬至，以為將來之範。

translations.literal: The new moon is the head of court assemblies; the qi is the beginning of growth; the new moon has the rite of announcing provisions, and the qi has the ceremony of suburban greeting—therefore Confucius fixed the calendar and established new-moon dawn and winter solstice as the model for the future.
translations.idiomatic: The new moon heads the court assembly; the seasonal node marks the start of growth. The new moon has its rite of announcing provisions; the node has its suburban greeting ceremony. Confucius therefore fixed the calendar and established new-moon dawn and winter solstice as the model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 今孝孫曆法，並按明文，以月行遲疾定其合朔，欲今食必在朔，不在晦、二之日也。

translations.literal: Now Xiaosun's calendrical method follows the explicit texts, using the moon's slow and fast motion to fix conjunction, wishing that eclipses must fall on the new moon and not on the last day or second day.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun's calendar follows the explicit texts, using the moon's anomalistic motion to fix conjunction so that eclipses fall on the new moon, not on the last or second day of the month.

sentences.zh: 縱使頻月一小、三大，得天之統。

translations.literal: Even if frequently one small month and three large months occur in a month, this attains Heaven's unity.
translations.idiomatic: Even if months frequently alternate one short and three long, this accords with Heaven's unity.

sentences.zh: 大抵其法有三，今列之雲。

translations.literal: In general its method has three parts; they are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The method has three parts in all, listed below.

sentences.zh: 第一，勘日食證恆在朔。

translations.literal: First: verify that solar eclipses constantly fall on the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: First: verify that solar eclipses always fall on the new moon.

sentences.zh: 引《詩》雲：「十月之交，朔日辛卯，日有食之。」

translations.literal: It cites the Odes: "At the crossing of the tenth month, on the xinmao day of the new moon, the sun was eclipsed."
translations.idiomatic: It cites the Odes: "At the crossing of the tenth month, on the xinmao day of the new moon, the sun was eclipsed."

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆術推算，符合不差。

translations.literal: Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, the match is exact without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, the match is exact.

sentences.zh: 《春秋經》書日食三十五。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records thirty-five solar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records thirty-five solar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 二十七日食，經書有朔，推與甲子元曆不差。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven eclipses—the classic records a new moon; calculation with the Jiazi Origin Calendar matches without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Of twenty-seven eclipses where the classic records a new moon, calculation with the Jiazi Origin Calendar matches exactly.

sentences.zh: 八食，經書並無朔字。

translations.literal: Eight eclipses—the classic records no new-moon character.
translations.idiomatic: Eight eclipses are recorded without the new-moon character.

sentences.zh: 《左氏傳》雲：「不書朔，官失之也。」

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "Not recording the new moon—an error of the officials."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "Failure to record the new moon was an error of the officials."

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》雲：「不言朔者，食二日也。」

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: "Not stating the new moon—the eclipse was on the second day."
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary says: "Failure to state the new moon means the eclipse was on the second day."

sentences.zh: 《谷梁傳》雲：「不言朔者，食晦也。」

translations.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: "Not stating the new moon—the eclipse was on the last day."
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang Commentary says: "Failure to state the new moon means the eclipse was on the last day."

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆推算，俱是朔日。

translations.literal: Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, all are new-moon days.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, all eight fall on new-moon days.

sentences.zh: 丘明受經夫子，于理尤詳，《公羊》、《谷梁》皆臆說也。

translations.literal: Qiu Ming received the classic from the Master and is especially detailed in principle; the Gongyang and Guliang are both speculative interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qiuming received the classic directly from Confucius and is far more reliable; the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries are speculative interpretations.

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏》隱公三年二月己巳，日有食之。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary of the Spring and Autumn Annals, third year of Duke Yin, second month, day jisi—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary, Duke Yin third year, second month, jisi day: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合己巳朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on jisi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the jisi day new moon.

sentences.zh: 莊公十八年春三月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang, eighteenth year, spring, third month—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang, year 18, spring, third month: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合壬子朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on renzi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the renzi day new moon.

sentences.zh: 僖公十二年三月庚午，日有食之。

translations.literal: Duke Xi, twelfth year, third month, day gengwu—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi, twelfth year, third month, gengwu day: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合庚午朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on gengwu new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the gengwu day new moon.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏五月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, summer, fifth month—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: fifteenth year of Year, summer, fifth month: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合癸未朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on guiwei new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the guiwei day new moon.

sentences.zh: 襄公十五年秋八月丁巳，日有食之。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang, fifteenth year, autumn, eighth month, day dingsi—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang, year 15, autumn, eighth month, dingsi day: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合丁巳朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on dingsi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the dingsi day new moon.

sentences.zh: 前、後漢及魏、晉四代所記日食，朔、晦及先晦，都合一百八十一，今以甲子元曆術推之，併合朔日而食。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses recorded by the Former and Later Han and the Wei and Jin over four dynasties, on new moon, last day, and day before last day—in all one hundred eighty-one; now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, all match new-moon-day eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The 181 solar eclipses recorded by the Former and Later Han, Wei, and Jin—whether dated to new moon, last day, or day before last—all calculate as new-moon eclipses under the Jiazi Origin Calendar.

sentences.zh: 前漢合有四十五食。

translations.literal: Former Han in all had forty-five eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Han recorded forty-five eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 三食並先晦一日，三十二食並皆晦日，十食並是朔日

translations.literal: Three eclipses were all one day before the last day; thirty-two eclipses were all on the last day; ten eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Three fell one day before the last day; thirty-two on the last day; ten on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 後漢合有七十四食。

translations.literal: Later Han in all had seventy-four eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han recorded seventy-four eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 三十七食並皆晦日，三十七食並皆朔日

translations.literal: Thirty-seven eclipses were all on the last day; thirty-seven eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven fell on the last day; thirty-seven on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 魏合有十四食。

translations.literal: Wei in all had fourteen eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Wei recorded fourteen eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 四食並皆晦日，十食並皆朔日

translations.literal: Four eclipses were all on the last day; ten eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Four fell on the last day; ten on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 晉合有四十八食。

translations.literal: Jin in all had forty-eight eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Jin recorded forty-eight eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 二十五食並皆晦日，二十三食並皆朔日

translations.literal: Twenty-five eclipses were all on the last day; twenty-three eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five fell on the last day; twenty-three on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 第二，勘度差變驗。

translations.literal: Second: verify the changing discrepancy in degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Second: verify the changing discrepancy in celestial degrees.

sentences.zh: 《尚書》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "The days are short and the star Mao culminates, marking mid-winter."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "The days are short and the star Mao culminates, marking mid-winter."

sentences.zh: 即是唐堯之時，冬至之日，日在危宿，合昏之時，昴正午。

translations.literal: This was in the time of Tang Yao: on the winter solstice the sun was in the Wei lodge; at dusk Mao was on the meridian.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the time of Emperor Yao of Tang: on the winter solstice the sun was in the Wei lodge, and at dusk Mao was on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 案《竹書紀年》，堯元年丙子。

translations.literal: According to the Bamboo Annals, Yao's first year was bingzi.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Bamboo Annals, Yao's first year was bingzi.

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆術推算得合堯時冬至之日，合昏之時，昴星正午。

translations.literal: Calculating now by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, the winter solstice day in Yao's time and Mao on the meridian at dusk match exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, the winter solstice in Yao's time and Mao on the meridian at dusk match exactly.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》武帝太初元年丁丑歲，落下閎等考定太初曆冬至之日，日在牽牛初。

translations.literal: The History of Han records that in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, dingchou year, Luoxia Hong and others fixed the winter solstice day of the Taichu Calendar, with the sun at the beginning of Qianniu.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han records that in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu (dingchou), Luoxia Hong and others fixed the Taichu Calendar winter solstice, with the sun at the beginning of the Qianniu lodge.

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆術算，即得斗末牛初矣。

translations.literal: Calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method now, one obtains the end of Dipper and beginning of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, one obtains the end of the Dipper lodge and beginning of the Ox lodge.

sentences.zh: 晉時有薑岌，又以月食驗於日度，知冬至之日日在斗十七度。

translations.literal: In Jin there was Jiang Ji, who also verified solar degree by lunar eclipse and knew the winter solstice sun was at the seventeenth degree of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Jiang Ji verified solar longitude by lunar eclipse and found the winter solstice sun at the seventeenth degree of the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十年癸酉歲，何承天考驗乾度，亦知冬至之日日在斗十七度。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, guiyou year, He Chengtian verified the celestial degree and likewise knew the winter solstice sun was at the seventeenth degree of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song (guiyou), He Chengtian verified celestial longitude and likewise found the winter solstice sun at the seventeenth degree of the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 雖言冬至後上三日，前後通融，只合在斗十七度。

translations.literal: Although it is said the winter solstice was reported three days later, reconciling before and after, it should only be at the seventeenth degree of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Although the winter solstice was reported three days late, reconciling the accounts, it should still fall at the seventeenth degree of the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 但堯年漢日，所在既殊，唯晉及宋，所在未改，故知其度，理有變差。

translations.literal: But Yao's year and Han's day differ in position; only Jin and Song did not change position, so one knows the degree has naturally shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's epoch and Han's day differ in solar position; only Jin and Song remained unchanged, showing that the degree has naturally shifted over time.

sentences.zh: 至今大隋甲辰之歲，考定歷數象，以稽天道，知冬至之日日在斗十三度。

translations.literal: Down to the jiachen year of Great Sui, verifying calendrical numbers and images against the Way of Heaven, we know the winter solstice sun is at the thirteenth degree of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the jiachen year of Great Sui, verifying calendrical reckoning against the Way of Heaven, we know the winter solstice sun is at the thirteenth degree of the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 第三，勘氣影長驗。

translations.literal: Third: verify by qi and shadow length.
translations.idiomatic: Third: verify by seasonal nodes and gnomon shadow length.

sentences.zh: 《春秋緯命曆序》雲：「魯僖公五年正月壬子朔旦冬至。」

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Apocrypha, Calendar Sequence Command, says: "In the fifth year of Duke Xi of Lu, first month, day renzi, new-moon dawn, winter solstice."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Apocrypha, Calendar Sequence Command, states: "Duke Xi of Lu, fifth year, first month, renzi day, new-moon dawn, winter solstice."

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆術推算，得合不差。

translations.literal: Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, the match is exact without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, the match is exact.

sentences.zh: 《宋書》元嘉十年，何承天以土圭測影，知冬至已差三日。

translations.literal: The History of Song: in the tenth year of Yuanjia, He Chengtian measured shadows with the earth gnomon and knew the winter solstice had already differed by three days.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Song records that in tenth year of Yuanjia, He Chengtian measured shadows with an earth gnomon and found the winter solstice had already drifted by three days.

sentences.zh: 詔使付外考驗，起元嘉十三年為始，畢元嘉二十年，八年之中，冬至之日恆與影長之日差校三日。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent out for verification, beginning from the thirteenth year of Yuanjia and ending in the twentieth year of Yuanjia; within eight years, on winter solstice days it constantly differed from the longest-shadow days by three days upon comparison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered external verification from thirteenth year of Yuanjia through 20th year of Yuanjia; over eight years, winter solstice consistently differed from the longest-shadow day by three days.

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆術推算，但是冬至之日恆與影長之符合不差。

translations.literal: Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, on every winter solstice day it constantly matches the longest-shadow day without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, every winter solstice matches the longest-shadow day exactly.
