sentences.zh: 于時新曆初頒，賓有寵于高祖，劉暉附會之，被升為太史令。

translations.literal: At that time the new calendar had just been promulgated; Bin enjoyed Gaozu's favor, and Liu Hui attached himself to him and was promoted to Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar had just been promulgated. Zhang Bin enjoyed Gaozu's favor, and Liu Hui attached himself to Bin and was promoted to Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 二人協議，共短孝孫，言其非毀天曆，率意迂怪，焯又妄相扶證，惑亂時人。

translations.literal: The two men joined in agreement to disparage Xiaosun together, saying he slandered and destroyed the celestial calendar, willfully making perverse and strange claims; Chuo also falsely supported and verified this, confusing the people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The two men colluded to attack Liu Xiaosun, accusing him of slandering the official calendar and making willfully eccentric claims. Liu Chuo falsely backed them, sowing confusion among scholars of the day.

sentences.zh: 孝孫、焯等，竟以他事斥罷。

translations.literal: Xiaosun, Chuo, and the others were ultimately dismissed on other charges.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun, Liu Chuo, and their allies were ultimately dismissed on other pretexts.

sentences.zh: 後賓死，孝孫為掖縣丞，委官入京，又上，前後為劉暉所詰，事寢不行。

translations.literal: Later, when Bin died, Xiaosun was Assistant Magistrate of Ye County; he resigned his office and entered the capital, submitting memorials again and again, but was repeatedly challenged by Liu Hui, and the matter was abandoned without implementation.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Bin's death, Liu Xiaosun, then Assistant Magistrate of Ye County, resigned and went to the capital to submit his calendar again. Liu Hui repeatedly blocked him, and the proposal went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 仍留孝孫直太史，累年不調，寓宿觀台。

translations.literal: Xiaosun was still retained as a direct appointee of the Grand Astrologer's office, unrewarded with promotion for many years, lodging at the Observational Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun remained attached to the Grand Astrologer's office as a direct appointee, unrewarded for years, lodging at the Observational Platform.

sentences.zh: 乃抱其書，弟子輿櫬，來詣闕下，伏而慟哭。

translations.literal: He then embraced his writings; his disciples carried his coffin and came to the palace gates, prostrating themselves and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought his writings; his disciples carried his coffin to the palace gates, where he prostrated himself and wept.

sentences.zh: 執法拘以奏之，高祖異焉，以問國子祭酒何妥。

translations.literal: The law officers detained him and reported this; Gaozu was struck by it and asked the Director of the Imperial Academy, He Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Law officers detained him and reported to the throne. Gaozu was moved and consulted Director of the Imperial Academy He Tuo.

sentences.zh: 妥言其善，即日擢授大都督，遣與賓曆比校短長。

translations.literal: Tuo said it was good; that very day Xiaosun was promoted to Grand Commander and sent to compare his calendar with Bin's for strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: He Tuo endorsed the work, and Liu Xiaosun was immediately promoted to Grand Commander and ordered to compare his calendar with Zhang Bin's.

sentences.zh: 先是信都人張胄玄，以算術直太史，久未知名。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Zhouxuan of Xindu, skilled in computation, served directly under the Grand Astrologer and had long been unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Zhouxuan of Xindu, skilled in computation, had served under the Grand Astrologer in obscurity for years.

sentences.zh: 至是與孝孫共短賓曆，異論鋒起，久之不定。

translations.literal: At this time he joined Xiaosun in disparaging Bin's calendar; conflicting opinions flared up and long remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Now he joined Liu Xiaosun in attacking Zhang Bin's calendar. Conflicting opinions multiplied and remained unresolved for a long time.

sentences.zh: 至十四年七月，上令參問日食事。

translations.literal: By the seventh month of the fourteenth year, the emperor ordered an inquiry into solar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of fourteenth year of Kaihuang, the emperor ordered an inquiry into solar eclipse predictions.

sentences.zh: 楊素等奏：「太史凡奏日食二十有五，唯一晦三朔，依克而食，尚不得其時，又不知所起，他皆無驗。

translations.literal: Yang Su and others memorialized: "The Grand Astrologer in all submitted twenty-five solar eclipses; only one on the last day and three on new moons, according to prediction and eclipse, still missed the correct time and did not know where they began; the rest were all unverified.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and others reported: "The Grand Astrologer's office submitted twenty-five eclipse predictions. Only four—one on the last day and three on new moons—even roughly matched the event, and those missed the correct hour and origin. The rest failed entirely.

sentences.zh: 胄玄所克，前後妙衷，時起分數，合如符契。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's predictions, before and after, were subtly accurate; the times and fractional parts matched like tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's predictions were consistently accurate; the times and fractional parts matched like tally and seal.

sentences.zh: 孝孫所克，驗亦過半。」

translations.literal: Xiaosun's predictions were verified in more than half the cases."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun's predictions were verified in more than half the cases."

sentences.zh: 於是高祖引孝孫、胄玄等，親自勞徠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozu summoned Xiaosun, Zhouxuan, and the others and personally received and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then summoned Liu Xiaosun, Zhang Zhouxuan, and the others and personally received them.

sentences.zh: 孝孫因請先斬劉暉，乃可定曆。

translations.literal: Xiaosun therefore requested that Liu Hui be executed first before the calendar could be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun then demanded that Liu Hui be executed before the calendar could be fixed.

sentences.zh: 高祖不懌，又罷之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was displeased and dismissed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was displeased and dismissed him again.

sentences.zh: 俄而孝孫卒，楊素、牛弘等傷惜之，又薦胄玄。

translations.literal: Soon Xiaosun died; Yang Su, Niu Hong, and others grieved for him and again recommended Zhouxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun soon died. Yang Su, Niu Hong, and others mourned him and again recommended Zhang Zhouxuan.

sentences.zh: 上召見之，胄玄因言日長影短之事，高祖大悅，賞賜甚厚，令與參定新術。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and received him; Zhouxuan spoke on the matter of longer days and shorter shadows, and Gaozu was greatly pleased, richly rewarding him and ordering him to participate in fixing the new method.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhang Zhouxuan, who spoke on the lengthening of days and shortening of shadows. Gaozu was greatly pleased, richly rewarded him, and ordered him to help fix the new calendar.

sentences.zh: 劉焯聞胄玄進用，又增損孝孫曆法，更名《七曜新術》，以奏之。

translations.literal: When Chuo heard that Zhouxuan had been promoted, he again added to and reduced Xiaosun's calendrical method, renaming it the "New Method of the Seven Luminaries," and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chuo learned of Zhang Zhouxuan's promotion, he revised Liu Xiaosun's calendar, renamed it the New Method of the Seven Luminaries, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 與胄玄之法，頗相乖爽，袁充與胄玄害之。

translations.literal: Compared with Zhouxuan's method, it was largely at variance; Yuan Chong and Zhouxuan harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: It diverged significantly from Zhang Zhouxuan's method. Yuan Chong and Zhang Zhouxuan worked against him.

sentences.zh: 焯又罷。

translations.literal: Chuo was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chuo was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，胄玄曆成，奏之。

translations.literal: By the seventeenth year, Zhouxuan's calendar was completed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By 17th year of Kaihuang, Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was complete and submitted.

sentences.zh: 上付楊素等校其短長。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted it to Yang Su and others to compare its strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted it to Yang Su and others to evaluate its merits.

sentences.zh: 劉暉與國子助教王頍等執舊曆術，迭相駁難，與司曆劉宜援據古史影等，駁胄玄雲：

translations.literal: Liu Hui and the Academy Assistant Instructor Wang Yi and others held to the old calendrical method, mutually refuting and challenging; together with Calendar Officer Liu Yi they drew on ancient histories and shadow records to refute Zhouxuan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and Academy Assistant Instructor Wang Yi defended the old calendar, trading refutations with Zhang Zhouxuan. Calendar Officer Liu Yi drew on ancient histories and shadow records to challenge him, stating:

sentences.zh: 《命曆序》僖公五年天正壬子朔旦日至，《左氏傳》僖公五年正月辛亥朔日南至。

translations.literal: The Calendar Sequence Command: fifth year of Duke Xi, celestial first month, day renzi, new-moon dawn, sun reaches extreme. The Zuo Commentary: fifth year of Duke Xi, first month, day xinhai, new moon, sun reaches south extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Sequence Command records Duke Xi's fifth year, celestial first month, renzi day, new-moon dawn, winter solstice. The Zuo Commentary records Duke Xi's fifth year, first month, xinhai day, new moon, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆，天正壬子朔冬至，合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, day renzi new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Commentary by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, renzi day new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，天正壬子朔，合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, day renzi new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Commentary by one day;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, renzi day new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day;

sentences.zh: 三日甲寅冬至，差《命曆序》二日，差《傳》三日。

translations.literal: Third day, day jiayin, winter solstice—differs from the Calendar Sequence Command by two days, from the Commentary by three days.
translations.idiomatic: Third day, jiayin, winter solstice—off by two days from the Calendar Sequence Command, three from the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 成公十二年，《命曆序》天正辛卯朔旦日至。

translations.literal: Twelfth year of Duke Cheng: the Calendar Sequence Command has celestial first month, day xinmao, new-moon dawn, sun reaches extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cheng, year 12: the Calendar Sequence Command records celestial first month, xinmao day new-moon dawn, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆，天正辛卯朔冬至，合《命曆序》。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, day xinmao new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, xinmao day new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，天正辛卯朔，合《命曆序》；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, day xinmao new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, xinmao day new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command;

sentences.zh: 二日壬辰冬至，差《命曆序》一日。

translations.literal: Second day, day renchen, winter solstice—differs from the Calendar Sequence Command by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Second day, renchen, winter solstice—off by one day from the Calendar Sequence Command.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十年，《春秋左氏傳》二月己丑朔日南至，准《命曆序》庚寅朔旦日至。

translations.literal: Twentieth year of Duke Zhao: the Zuo Commentary of the Spring and Autumn Annals, second month, day jichou new moon, sun reaches south extreme; according to the Calendar Sequence Command, day gengyin new-moon dawn, sun reaches extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao, year 20: the Zuo Commentary records second month, jichou day new moon, winter solstice; the Calendar Sequence Command records gengyin day new-moon dawn, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆，天正庚寅朔冬至，併合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, day gengyin new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command together, differs from the Commentary by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, gengyin day new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，天正庚寅朔，合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, day gengyin new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Commentary by one day;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, gengyin day new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day;

sentences.zh: 二日辛卯冬至，差《命曆序》一日，差《傳》二日。

translations.literal: Second day, day xinmao, winter solstice—differs from the Calendar Sequence Command by one day, from the Commentary by two days.
translations.idiomatic: Second day, xinmao, winter solstice—off by one day from the Calendar Sequence Command, two from the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 宜案《命曆序》及《春秋左氏傳》，並閏餘盡之歲，皆須朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: Yi finds that according to the Calendar Sequence Command and the Zuo Commentary of the Spring and Autumn Annals, in all years when the intercalary remainder is exhausted, new-moon dawn and winter solstice are required.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi argues that according to the Calendar Sequence Command and the Zuo Commentary, in every year when the intercalary remainder is exhausted, new-moon dawn and winter solstice must coincide.

sentences.zh: 若依《命曆序》勘《春秋》三十七食，合處至多；

translations.literal: If one verifies the thirty-seven eclipses of the Spring and Autumn Annals according to the Calendar Sequence Command, the matches are very numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Checking the Spring and Autumn Annals' thirty-seven eclipses against the Calendar Sequence Command yields numerous matches;

sentences.zh: 若依《左傳》，合者至少，是以知《傳》為錯。

translations.literal: if according to the Zuo Commentary, the matches are very few—therefore one knows the Commentary is in error.
translations.idiomatic: checking against the Zuo Commentary yields very few—proving the Commentary is in error.

sentences.zh: 今張胄玄信情置閏，《命曆序》及《傳》氣朔並差。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Zhouxuan arbitrarily sets intercalation according to his own judgment; the qi and new moons of the Calendar Sequence Command and the Commentary all differ.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan arbitrarily sets intercalation by personal judgment; the seasonal nodes and new moons diverge from both the Calendar Sequence Command and the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 又宋元嘉冬至影有七，張賓曆合者五，差者二，亦在前一日。

translations.literal: Also in Yuanjia of Liu Song there were seven winter-solstice shadow records; Zhang Bin's calendar matched five and missed two, both one day early.
translations.idiomatic: Of seven Yuanjia-era winter-solstice shadow records, Zhang Bin's calendar matched five and missed two—both one day early.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆合者三，差者四，在後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched three and missed four, all one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched three and missed four—all one day late.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年十一月甲寅朔，十五日戊辰冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Twelfth year of Yuanjia, eleventh month, day jiayin new moon; fifteenth day, day wuchen, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth year of Yuanjia, eleventh month, jiayin day new moon; fifteenth day, wuchen, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合戊辰冬至，張胄玄曆己巳冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches wuchen winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has jisi winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: wuchen winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: jisi winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 十三年十一月己酉朔，二十六日甲戌冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, eleventh month, day jiyou new moon; twenty-sixth day, day jiaxu, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: thirteenth year of Yuanjia, eleventh month, jiyou day new moon; twenty-sixth day, jiaxu, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 建德四年四月大、乙酉朔，三十日甲寅，月晨見東方。

translations.idiomatic: fourth year of Jiande, fourth month (long), yiyou day new moon; thirtieth day, jiayin—the moon was visible in the morning eastern sky.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆四月大、乙酉朔，三十日甲寅，月晨見東方，張胄玄曆四月小、乙酉朔，五月大，甲寅朔，月晨見東方。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: fourth month long, day yiyou new moon; thirtieth day, day jiayin—the moon was seen in the morning in the east. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fourth month short, day yiyou new moon; fifth month long, day jiayin new moon—the moon was seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: fourth month (long), yiyou new moon; day 30, jiayin—morning moon in the east. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fourth month (short), yiyou new moon; fifth month (long), jiayin new moon—morning moon in the east.

sentences.zh: 宜案影極長為冬至，影極短為夏至，二至自古史分可勘者二十四，其二十一有影，三有至日無影。

translations.literal: Yi finds that the longest shadow marks winter solstice and the shortest shadow marks summer solstice; of twenty-four solstices verifiable from ancient histories, twenty-one have shadow records and three have solstice days without shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi argues that the longest shadow marks winter solstice and the shortest marks summer solstice. Of twenty-four solstices verifiable from ancient records, twenty-one have shadow data and three record the solstice day without shadow measurements.

sentences.zh: 見行曆合一十八，差者六。

translations.literal: The calendar in use matched eighteen; six differed.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar then in use matched eighteen cases; six did not.

sentences.zh: 旅騎尉張胄玄曆合者八，差者一十六，二差後二日，一十四差後一日。

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched eight; sixteen differed—two two days late, fourteen one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched eight cases and missed sixteen—two by two days, fourteen by one day.

sentences.zh: 又開皇四年，在洛州測冬至影，與京師二處，進退絲毫不差。

translations.literal: Also in Kaihuang 4, winter solstice shadows were measured at Luoyang and the capital; at both places the advance and retreat matched to the slightest hair without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: fourth year of In of Kaihuang, winter solstice shadows measured at Luoyang and the capital agreed to the finest precision at both locations.

sentences.zh: 周天和已來案驗並在後。

translations.literal: From Tianhe of Zhou onward, verified cases all fall later.
translations.idiomatic: From Northern Zhou's Tianhe era onward, all verified cases fall one day late.

sentences.zh: 更檢得建德四年，晦朔東見；

translations.literal: Further checking found Jiande 4, last day of month, new moon, morning sighting in the east;
translations.idiomatic: Further review found fourth year of Jiande: on the last day of the month at new moon, the moon was sighted in the morning east;

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，五月朔日，月晨見東方。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fifth month new-moon day—the moon was seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fifth-month new-moon day—the moon visible in the morning east.

sentences.zh: 今十七年，張賓曆閏七月，張胄玄曆閏五月。

translations.literal: Also examining year seventeen: Zhang Bin's calendar has intercalary seventh month; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has intercalary fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Examining 17th year of Kaihuang: Zhang Bin's calendar places the intercalary month in the seventh month; Zhang Zhouxuan's in the fifth.

sentences.zh: 又審至以定閏，胄玄曆至既不當，故知置閏必乖。

translations.literal: Also, since intercalation is determined by the solstice, and Zhouxuan's calendar misses the solstice, one knows his intercalary placement must be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Since intercalation should be determined by the solstice, and Zhang Zhouxuan's solstice is wrong, his intercalary placement must be incorrect.

sentences.zh: 見行曆四月、五月頻大，張胄玄曆九月、十月頻大，為胄玄朔弱，頻大在後晨，故朔日殘月晨見東方。

translations.literal: The calendar in use frequently has long fourth and fifth months; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar frequently has long ninth and tenth months—because Zhouxuan's new moons are weak, with frequent long months in later mornings, hence on new-moon day the waning moon is seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The official calendar frequently assigns long fourth and fifth months; Zhang Zhouxuan's frequently assigns long ninth and tenth months. His new-moon reckoning is weak, producing long months in later morning hours—hence the waning moon appears in the eastern morning sky on new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 宜又案開皇四年十二月十五日癸卯，依曆月行在鬼三度，時加酉，月在卯上，食十五分之九，虧起西北。

translations.literal: Yi also cites Kaihuang 4, twelfth month, fifteenth day, day guimao: according to the calendar the moon was at three degrees of Ghost; hour added you; the moon was above mao; eclipse nine fifteenths; obscuration began northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi also cites fourth year of Kaihuang, twelfth month, day 15 (guimao): per the calendar the moon was at 3° Ghost; hour you; moon above mao; eclipse magnitude 9/15; obscuration began in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，一更一籌起食東北角，十五分之十，至四籌還生，至二更一籌複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: at the first watch, first tally, obscuration began at the northeast corner, ten fifteenths; by the fourth tally it was restored; by the second watch, first tally, fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: at the first watch, first tally, obscuration began at the northeast limb, magnitude 10/15; restored by the fourth tally; fully restored by the second watch, first tally.

sentences.zh: 五年六月三十日，依曆太陽虧，日在七星六度，加時在午少強上，食十五分之一半強，虧起西南角。

translations.literal: Fifth year, sixth month, thirtieth day: according to the calendar the sun was eclipsed; the sun at six degrees of Seven Stars; hour of occurrence at wu slightly strong; eclipse one and a half fifteenths strong; obscuration began southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: fifth year of Kaihuang, sixth month, day 30: per the calendar, solar eclipse; sun at 6° Seven Stars; hour of occurrence mid-wu; magnitude 1.5/15; obscuration began at the southwest limb.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，日乃在午後六刻上始食，虧起西北角，十五分之六，至未後一刻還生，至五刻複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the sun began eclipsing after the sixth quarter of wu; obscuration began northwest corner, six fifteenths; restored after the first quarter of wei; fully restored by the fifth quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: eclipse began after the sixth quarter-hour of wu; obscuration from the northwest, magnitude 6/15; restoration began after the first quarter of wei; full restoration by the fifth quarter.

sentences.zh: 六年六月十五日，依曆太陰虧，加時酉，在卯上，食十五分之九半弱，虧起西南，當其時陰雲不見月。

translations.literal: Sixth year, sixth month, fifteenth day: according to the calendar the moon was eclipsed; hour added you; above mao; eclipse nine and a half fifteenths weak; obscuration began southwest; at the time clouds hid the moon.
translations.idiomatic: sixth year of Kaihuang, sixth month, day 15: per the calendar, lunar eclipse; hour you; moon above mao; magnitude 9.5/15; obscuration from the southwest; clouds obscured the moon at the time.

sentences.zh: 至辰巳，雲裡見月，已食三分之二，虧從東北，既還雲合。

translations.literal: By chen and si, the moon was seen through clouds, already two-thirds eclipsed; obscuration from the northeast; after totality clouds closed again.
translations.idiomatic: By chen-si hours the moon appeared through clouds, already two-thirds eclipsed from the northeast; after totality clouds closed again.

sentences.zh: 至巳午間稍生，至午後，雲裡暫見，已複滿。

translations.literal: By si-wu it slightly restored; by afternoon clouds briefly parted—the moon was fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration began around si-wu; by afternoon a break in the clouds showed the moon fully restored.

sentences.zh: 十月三十日丁丑，依曆太陽虧，日在斗九度，時加在辰少弱上，食十五分之九強，虧起東北角。

translations.literal: Tenth month, thirtieth day, day dingchou: according to the calendar the sun was eclipsed; the sun at nine degrees of Dipper; hour added at chen slightly weak; eclipse nine fifteenths strong; obscuration began northeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, day 30 (dingchou): per the calendar, solar eclipse; sun at 9° Dipper; hour chen slightly weak; magnitude 9/15; obscuration from the northeast.

sentences.zh: 今候所見，日出山一丈，辰二刻始食，虧起正西，食三分之二，辰後二刻始生，入巳時三刻上複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the sun one zhang above the mountains at rise; eclipse began at the second quarter of chen; obscuration from due west, two-thirds eclipsed; restoration began after the second quarter of chen; fully restored entering the third quarter of si.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: sun one zhang above the horizon at sunrise; eclipse began at chen 2; obscuration from the west, two-thirds magnitude; restoration after chen 2; full restoration by si 3.

sentences.zh: 十年三月十六日癸卯，依曆月行在氐七度，時加戌，月在辰太半上，食十五分之七半強，虧起東北。

translations.literal: Tenth year, third month, sixteenth day, day guimao: according to the calendar the moon at seven degrees of Di; hour added xu; moon above chen greatly past midpoint; eclipse seven and a half fifteenths strong; obscuration began northeast.
translations.idiomatic: tenth year of Kaihuang, third month, day 16 (guimao): per the calendar moon at 7° Di; hour xu; moon well past chen; magnitude 7.5/15; obscuration from the northeast.

sentences.zh: 今候，月初出卯南，帶半食，出至辰初三分，可食二分許，漸生，辰未已複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the moon at month's first rising south of mao, half eclipsed; by the beginning of chen about two-thirds eclipsed; gradually restored; fully restored before wei.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: at first rising south of mao the moon was half eclipsed; by early chen about two-thirds; gradual restoration; fully restored before wei.

sentences.zh: 見行曆九月十六日庚子，月行在胃四度，時加醜，月在未半強上，食十分之三半強，虧起正東。

translations.literal: The calendar in use, ninth month, sixteenth day, day gengzi: moon at four degrees of Stomach; hour added chou; moon above wei half strong; eclipse three and a half tenths strong; obscuration began due east.
translations.idiomatic: Official calendar, ninth month, day 16 (gengzi): moon at 4° Stomach; hour chou; moon above wei; magnitude 3.5/10; obscuration from the east.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，月以午後二刻，食起正東，須臾如南，至未正上，食南畔五分之四，漸生，入申一刻半複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the moon at the second quarter after wu, eclipse began due east; shortly turning south; at the exact center of wei, four-fifths of the south limb eclipsed; gradually restored; fully restored entering the first and a half quarter of shen.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: eclipse began due east at the second quarter after wu; briefly turning south; at exact wei, four-fifths of the southern limb eclipsed; gradual restoration; full by shen 1.5.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月十五日己未，依曆月行在室七度，時加戌，月在辰太強上，食十五分之十二半弱，虧起西北。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, seventh month, fifteenth day, day jiwei: according to the calendar the moon at seven degrees of Room; hour added xu; moon above chen very strong; eclipse twelve and a half fifteenths weak; obscuration began northwest.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth year of Kaihuang, seventh month, day 15 (jiwei): per the calendar moon at 7° Room; hour xu; moon above chen; magnitude 12.5/15; obscuration from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，一更三籌起西北上，食准三分之二強，與曆注同。

translations.literal: Now observed: at the first watch, third tally, obscuration began northwest; eclipse about two-thirds strong—matching the calendar note.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: at the first watch, third tally, obscuration began northwest at about two-thirds magnitude—matching the calendar prediction.

sentences.zh: 十三年七月十六日，依曆月在申半強上，食十五分之半弱，虧起西南。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, seventh month, sixteenth day: according to the calendar the moon above shen half strong; eclipse half a fifteenth weak; obscuration began southwest.
translations.idiomatic: thirteenth year of Kaihuang, seventh month, day 16: per the calendar moon above shen; magnitude 0.5/15; obscuration from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 十五日夜，從四更候月，五更一籌起東北上，食半強，入雲不見。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth night, watching from the fourth watch—the moon at the first tally of the fifth watch began northeast; half strong eclipsed; entered clouds and was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the 15th, watching from the fourth watch: at the fifth watch, first tally, obscuration began northeast at half magnitude; then lost in clouds.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月一日，依歷時加巳弱上，食十五分之十二半強。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, seventh month, first day: according to the calendar hour added si weak; eclipse twelve and a half fifteenths strong.
translations.idiomatic: fourteenth year of Kaihuang, seventh month, day 1: per the calendar, hour si weak; magnitude 12.5/15.

sentences.zh: 至未後三刻，日乃食，虧起西北，食半許，入雲不見，食頃暫見，猶未複生，因即雲鄣。

translations.literal: By the third quarter after wei the sun was eclipsed; obscuration began northwest; about half eclipsed; entered clouds; briefly seen during the eclipse but not yet restored; then cloud-covered.
translations.idiomatic: By wei 3 the sun was eclipsed from the northwest at about half magnitude; lost in clouds; briefly visible during totality but not yet restored; then obscured again.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月十六日庚午，依曆月行在井十七度，時加亥，月在巳半上，食十五分之九半強，虧西北。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, eleventh month, sixteenth day, day gengwu: according to the calendar the moon at seventeen degrees of Well; hour added hai; moon above si half; eclipse nine and a half fifteenths strong; obscuration northwest.
translations.idiomatic: fifteenth year of Kaihuang, eleventh month, day 16 (gengwu): per the calendar moon at 17° Well; hour hai; moon above si; magnitude 9.5/15; obscuration northwest.

sentences.zh: 其夜一更四籌後，月在辰上起食，虧東南，至二更三籌，月在巳上，食三分之二許，漸生，至三更一籌，月在丙上，複滿。

translations.literal: That night after the first watch, fourth tally, the moon above chen began eclipsing; obscuration southeast; by the second watch, third tally, moon above si, about two-thirds eclipsed; gradually restored; by the third watch, first tally, moon above bing, fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: That night after the first watch, fourth tally: moon above chen, eclipse began southeast; by second watch, third tally, moon above si, about two-thirds; gradual restoration; by third watch, first tally, moon above bing, fully restored.

sentences.zh: 十六年十一月十六日乙丑，依曆月行在井十七度，時加醜，月在未太弱上，食十五分之十二半弱，虧起東南。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, eleventh month, sixteenth day, day yichou: according to the calendar the moon at seventeen degrees of Well; hour added chou; moon above wei very weak; eclipse twelve and a half fifteenths weak; obscuration began southeast.
translations.idiomatic: 16th year of Kaihuang, eleventh month, day 16 (yichou): per the calendar moon at 17° Well; hour chou; moon above wei; magnitude 12.5/15; obscuration from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 十五日夜伺候，至三更一籌，月在丙上，雲裡見，已食十五分之三許，虧起正東，至丁上，食既，後從東南生，至四更三籌，月在未末，複滿。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth night observed: by the third watch, first tally, moon above bing seen through clouds, already about three fifteenths eclipsed; obscuration began due east; at ding, totality; then restored from the southeast; by the fourth watch, third tally, moon at the end of wei, fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Observed on the night of the 15th: by third watch, first tally, moon above bing seen through clouds, already about 3/15 eclipsed from the east; totality at ding; restoration from the southeast; by fourth watch, third tally, moon at end of wei, fully restored.

sentences.zh: 而胄玄不能盡中。

translations.literal: Yet Zhouxuan could not fully hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Zhouxuan could not fully hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 迭相駁難，高祖惑焉，逾時不決。

translations.literal: They mutually refuted and challenged; Gaozu was perplexed, and for a long time no decision was made.
translations.idiomatic: The parties traded refutations until Gaozu was perplexed and no decision was reached for a long time.

sentences.zh: 會通事舍人顏慜楚上書雲：「漢落下閎改《顓頊曆》作《太初曆》，雲後八百歲，此曆差一日。」

translations.literal: Then Palace Attendant Yan Minting submitted a memorial, saying: "Under Han, Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar to make the Taichu Calendar, saying that after eight hundred years this calendar would differ by one day."
translations.idiomatic: Then Palace Attendant Yan Minting submitted a memorial: "Under the Han, Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar into the Taichu Calendar, declaring that after eight hundred years it would err by one day."

sentences.zh: 語在胄玄傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Zhouxuan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in Zhang Zhouxuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲神其事，遂下詔曰：「朕應運受圖，君臨萬宇，思欲興複聖教，恢弘令典，上順天道，下授人時，搜揚海內，廣延術士。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to make the matter miraculous and therefore issued an edict: "We have received the mandate and the chart, ruling the myriad realms, wishing to revive sage teaching and expand the great statutes, aligning above with the Way of Heaven and below granting the seasons to the people, searching within the seas and broadly extending to masters of technique.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to invest the matter with portentous significance and issued an edict: "Having received the mandate, We rule the realm, seeking to revive sage teaching and expand the statutes—aligning with Heaven above and granting the seasons to the people below, searching far and wide for masters of calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 旅騎尉張胄玄，理思沉敏，術藝宏深，懷道白首，來上曆法。

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Zhang Zhouxuan—his reasoning deep and keen, his arts vast and profound, devoted to the Way until white-haired age—came to submit a calendar method.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry Commandant Zhang Zhouxuan, deep of mind and vast in skill, devoted to the Way into old age, submitted his calendar method.

sentences.zh: 令與太史舊曆，並加勘審。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with the Grand Astrologer's old calendar jointly to examine and verify.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compare his calendar jointly with the Grand Astrologer's existing system.

sentences.zh: 仰觀玄象，參驗璿璣，胄玄歷數與七曜符合，太史所行，乃多疏舛，群官博議，咸以胄玄為密。

translations.literal: Looking up to observe the dark images and verifying against the armillary sphere, Zhouxuan's reckoning matched the seven luminaries; what the Grand Astrologer practiced was largely coarse and erroneous; the officials' broad deliberation all judged Zhouxuan as precise.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the heavens and verifying against the armillary sphere, Zhang Zhouxuan's reckoning matched the seven luminaries, while the Grand Astrologer's system was largely erroneous. The assembled officials judged Zhang Zhouxuan's method the more precise.

sentences.zh: 太史令劉暉，司曆郭翟、劉宜，驍騎尉任悅，往經修造，致此乖謬。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Liu Hui, Calendar Officers Guo Di and Liu Yi, and Cavalry Commandant Ren Yue—having previously revised and created—caused these errors.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Liu Hui, Calendar Officers Guo Di and Liu Yi, and Cavalry Commandant Ren Yue—who had previously devised the calendar—were responsible for these errors.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍、領太史令庾季才，太史丞邢俊，司曆郭遠，曆博士蘇粲，曆助教傅俊、成珍等，既是職司，須審疏密。

translations.literal: Direct Palace Attendant and Grand Astrologer Yu Jicai, Assistant Grand Astrologer Xing Jun, Calendar Officer Guo Yuan, Calendar Erudite Su Can, and Calendar Assistant Instructors Fu Jun and Cheng Zhen—as they were officers of duty, had to examine density and sparsity.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Palace Attendant and Grand Astrologer Yu Jicai, Assistant Grand Astrologer Xing Jun, Calendar Officer Guo Yuan, and Erudites Su Can, Fu Jun, and Cheng Zhen—as calendrical officers—should have reviewed the system's accuracy.

sentences.zh: 遂虛行此曆，無所發明。

translations.literal: Yet they vainly allowed this calendar to be used without any contribution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they allowed this faulty calendar to remain in use without objection.

sentences.zh: 論暉等情狀，已合科罪，方共飾非護短，不從正法。

translations.literal: Considering Hui and the others' circumstances, they already deserved punishment by law; yet they together embellished errors and shielded faults, not following correct law.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and his colleagues already deserved punishment; instead they embellished errors and shielded faults, defying proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 季才等附下罔上，義實難容。」

translations.literal: Jicai and the others attached themselves below to deceive above—the righteousness of this was hard to tolerate."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai and his colleagues deceived their superiors—conduct that could not be tolerated."

sentences.zh: 於是暉等四人，元造詐者，並除名；

translations.literal: Thereupon Hui and the other four men, the original fabricators of fraud, were all stripped of their names;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and three others, the original authors of the faulty calendar, were stripped of rank;

sentences.zh: 季才等六人，容隱奸慝，俱解見任。

translations.literal: Jicai and the other six men, who concealed wickedness, were all dismissed from their current posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai and five others, who had concealed the fraud, were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 胄玄所造曆法，付有司施行。

translations.literal: The calendar method created by Zhouxuan was entrusted to the relevant offices for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was entrusted to the relevant offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 擢拜胄玄為員外散騎侍郎，領太史令。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan was promoted and appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant, concurrently Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan was promoted to Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant and appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 胄玄進袁充，互相引重，各擅一能，更為延譽。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan recommended Yuan Chong; they mutually promoted each other, each excelling in one skill, and further extended each other's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan recommended Yuan Chong; they promoted each other, each claiming mastery in one area, and further burnished each other's reputations.

sentences.zh: 胄玄言充曆妙極前賢，充言胄玄曆術冠於今古。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan said Chong's calendar reached the subtle extreme of former sages; Chong said Zhouxuan's calendrical art topped all from ancient times to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan declared Yuan Chong's calendar the finest since antiquity; Yuan Chong declared Zhang Zhouxuan's calendrical art unmatched in all history.

sentences.zh: 胄玄學祖沖之，兼傳其師法。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan studied Zu Chongzhi and also transmitted his master's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan studied Zu Chongzhi and also transmitted his master's methods.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，克食頗中。

translations.literal: From this time forward, eclipse predictions largely hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: From this point forward, eclipse predictions largely hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 其開皇十七年所行曆術，命冬至起虛五度。

translations.literal: The calendrical method used from Kaihuang 17 set winter solstice beginning at five degrees of xu.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar adopted in 17th year of Kaihuang set the winter solstice at the fifth degree of the Xu lodge.

sentences.zh: 後稍覺其疏，至大業四年劉焯卒後，乃敢改法，命起虛七度，諸法率更有增損，朔終義寧。

translations.literal: Later it was gradually felt to be coarse; by Daye 4, after Liu Chuo's death, he dared to change the method, setting the beginning at seven degrees of xu; the various methods were generally further added to and reduced, continuing until Yining.
translations.idiomatic: Later its imprecision became apparent; by fourth year of Daye, after Liu Chuo's death, Zhang Zhouxuan revised the method to set the winter solstice at the seventh degree of Xu, with further adjustments to various parameters, continuing until the Yining era.

sentences.zh: 今錄戊辰年所定曆術著之於此雲。

translations.literal: Now the calendar method fixed in the wuchen year is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records the calendar method fixed in the wuchen year.

sentences.zh: 自甲子元至大業四年戊辰，百四十二萬七千六百四十四年，算外。

translations.literal: From the jiazi origin to Daye 4, wuchen, one million four hundred twenty-seven thousand six hundred forty-four years, outside the calculation.
translations.idiomatic: From the jiazi origin to fourth year of Daye (wuchen): 1,427,644 years beyond the epoch.

sentences.zh: 推積月術：

translations.literal: Method for computing accumulated months:
translations.idiomatic: Method for computing accumulated months:

sentences.zh: 置入元已來至所求年，以章月乘之，如章歲得一，為積月，餘為閏餘。

translations.literal: Set the count from the origin to the year sought; multiply by cycle month; divide by cycle year to get one—this gives accumulated months; the remainder is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: From the origin to the year sought, multiply by the cycle month and divide by the cycle year to obtain accumulated months; the remainder is the intercalary remainder.

sentences.zh: 閏餘三百九十七巳上，若冬至不在其月，加積月一

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is three hundred ninety-seven or above, and winter solstice is not in that month, add one to accumulated months.
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalary remainder is 397 or above and winter solstice does not fall in that month, add one to the accumulated months.

sentences.zh: 推月朔弦望術：

translations.literal: Method for computing new moon, first quarter, full moon, and last quarter:
translations.idiomatic: Method for computing new moon, first quarter, full moon, and last quarter:

sentences.zh: 以月法乘積月，如法得一，為積日，餘為小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply accumulated months by the month divisor; divide by the divisor to obtain one, yielding accumulated days; the remainder is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply accumulated months by the month divisor; divide by the divisor to obtain one, yielding accumulated days; the remainder is the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六十去積日，餘為大餘，命以甲子算外，為所求年天正月朔日。

translations.literal: Remove multiples of sixty from accumulated days; the remainder is the large remainder; count from jiazi beyond the tally—this is the new-moon day of the celestial first month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Remove multiples of sixty from accumulated days; the remainder is the large remainder; count from jiazi beyond the tally—this is the new-moon day of the celestial first month of the year sought.

sentences.zh: 天正月者，建子月也，今為去年十一月。

translations.literal: The celestial first month establishes zi—now taken as the eleventh month of the prior year.
translations.idiomatic: The celestial first month establishes zi—now taken as the eleventh month of the prior year.

sentences.zh: 凡朔小餘五百四十七巳上，其月大。

translations.literal: If the new-moon small remainder is 547 or above, the month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the new-moon small remainder is 547 or above, the month is long.

sentences.zh: 加大餘七，小餘四百三十七太；

translations.literal: Add seven to the large remainder and 437 plus three-quarters to the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Add seven to the large remainder and 437 plus three-quarters to the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 凡四分一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: One-quarter is "less," two-quarters is "half," three-quarters is "greater".
translations.idiomatic: One-quarter is "less," two-quarters is "half," three-quarters is "greater".

sentences.zh: 小餘滿日法去之，從大餘；

translations.literal: When the small remainder fills the day divisor, remove it and carry to the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: When the small remainder fills the day divisor, remove it and carry to the large remainder.

sentences.zh: 滿六十去之，命如前，為上弦日。

translations.literal: When it fills sixty, remove it; count as before—this is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: When it fills sixty, remove it; count as before—this is the first-quarter day.

sentences.zh: 又加，得望、下弦、後月朔。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add again to obtain full moon, last quarter, and the next month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 朔餘滿五百三十七，其月大，減者小餘。

translations.literal: If the new-moon remainder fills 537, the month is long; if reduced, use the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: If the new-moon remainder fills 537, the month is long; if reduced, use the small remainder.

translations.literal: Method for computing the twenty-four qi:
translations.idiomatic: Method for computing the twenty-four qi:

translations.literal: multiply by month divisor intercalary remainder, cycle year small remainder,, divide by qi divisor to obtain one,, count from new moon beyond tally, Winter Solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by month divisor intercalary remainder, cycle year small remainder,, divide by qi divisor to obtain one,, count from new moon beyond tally, Winter Solstice.

sentences.zh: 不盡者，以十一約之，為日分。

translations.idiomatic: Divide remainder by eleven for day fractions.

translations.idiomatic: Small fraction 8 carries to day fraction, day fraction full carries to days.
